correctness.rationale: Im(R) is a subalgebra by the weight-zero identity. A nonzero finite-dimensional commutative reduced subalgebra contains a nonzero idempotent, using unitization and the product-of-fields structure of Artinian reduced rings. If e=R(x) is such an idempotent, e=R(2ex); characteristic two gives e=0 immediately, while otherwise R(ex)=e/2 and a second Rota-Baxter application gives e/4=e/2. Thus R=0 in all characteristics. The group-algebra corollary follows from Maschke plus commutativity. The embedded checker verifies split reduced cases and the square-zero boundary.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a structural vanishing criterion on a broad natural class, sharp against the standard square-zero construction. It strengthens a known nilpotence theorem to exact zero on reduced commutative algebras in every characteristic and settles an explicit group-algebra question for all finite abelian groups in nonmodular characteristic, not just prime cyclic groups.
